title: The Structural Rentier Asset
existing_coverage: No existing coverage of this paper or author. The wiki has substantial adjacent theory at concepts/rentier.md (Hudson, Mazzucato, Keynes's 'euthanasia of the rentier'), concepts/financialization-of-land.md (the mortgage-credit/land-price collateral feedback loop, Ryan-Collins et al.), and research/christophers-rentier-capitalism.md, but nothing on a formal no-steady-state/Minsky-correction model of a 'structural rentier asset.'

It's a working paper, not peer-reviewed — the author (Henry Fudge) is a former wealth manager turned Substack/TikTok commentator publishing under the 'Rentier Black Hole' brand — so this should be flagged as a preprint/non-peer-reviewed source, not treated with the confidence of a journal article.
source_notes: Henry Fudge, SSRN Electronic Journal (2026), working paper (not peer-reviewed). Defines a 'structural rentier asset' as one whose supply elasticity toward capital inflow tends to zero; if it also serves as bank collateral and receives preferential tax treatment, risk-adjusted return diverges monotonically from productive assets with no interior steady state, ending in policy intervention or a Minsky correction, while productive capital is crowded out and GDP mismeasurement hides the shrinking productive base. Author is a public-facing 'Rentier Black Hole' commentator (Substack, TikTok, prior related SSRN paper 'The Housing Theory of Everything'), not a traditional academic — note this when drafting.

title: The Unseen Thread: The Influence of Henry George on Early Chinese Communist Leaders—The Case of Li Dazhao

The authors are explicit that the connection is thematic/parallel rather than documented direct citation ('despite the absence of direct citations'), so this should be graded honestly as a C/D-claim, similar to how the wiki already flags the Sun Yat-sen companion paper's abstract-only status.
source_notes: Baoqin Meng, Yanfang Han, Junfeng Wang & Xiaoqi Guan, American Journal of Economics and Sociology (published online 2025-12-31).
